nodes.label: Design-tree interview guide
nodes.rationale: Use during Phase 3. Pick the next unresolved branch whose dependencies are satisfied, ask one focused question, and confirm before moving on.

nodes.label: Branch 1 Problem and success
nodes.rationale: Root branch that unlocks the others. Exit is a one-sentence problem statement plus measurable 30/90 day goals the user confirms, including what is explicitly not success.

nodes.label: Branch 2 Users and permissions
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branch 1. Exit is an agreed role by permission matrix.

nodes.label: Branch 3 Product surface and scope
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branch 1. Exit is confirmed in-scope and out-of-scope lists, including MVP and cross-cutting token, Caddy, and Docker questions.

nodes.label: Branch 4 Data and integrations
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 2–3. Exit is an entity list and agreed integration boundaries, checked against Phase 2 models, serializers, and API routes.

nodes.label: Branch 5 UX and flows
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 2–4. Exit is a numbered primary flow, listed edge cases, and a design reference or match-existing note. i18n is called out for the IHCS website only.

nodes.label: Branch 6 Non-functional requirements
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 3–5. Covers performance, accessibility, security, and reliability, or an explicit statement of no special requirements.

nodes.label: Branch 7 Rollout and phasing
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 3–5. Exit is a phased delivery table or a single-release confirmation, including feature flags and client sign-off.

nodes.label: Branch 8 Acceptance and verification
nodes.rationale: Depends on all prior branches. Convert decisions into per-role manual tests, API method/path/status expectations, and regression areas that prove Branch 1 success.

nodes.label: Role and permission matrix
nodes.rationale: Example roles in the guide are public visitor, ES admin, DS manager, kiosk player, and API consumer. Auth examples include an existing token flow, a new login, SSO, and anonymous access.

nodes.label: Interview product surfaces
nodes.rationale: The guide asks whether the product is the IHCS marketing site, Email Signatures, Digital Signage, or backend-only. Those names are what this file says. They conflict with Care Bear Daycare in the brand reference.

nodes.label: Auth checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Cross-check Phase 2 against middleware.ts, AdminAuthGuard, and DRF permissions.

nodes.label: External systems
nodes.rationale: Integration examples named in the guide: Entra, Outlook add-in, WebSockets, and third-party APIs.

nodes.label: Module sketch guide
nodes.rationale: Architecture sketching during Phase 4, after the design-tree interview and before the PRD. Map requirements to concrete modules and confirm the sketch with the user.

nodes.label: Deep module criteria
nodes.rationale: One responsibility, dependencies passed as plain data, testable as inputs to outputs without a database or browser, and a stable function or small-class API. Mark Deep isolated tests versus Shallow integration or UI tests.

nodes.label: Monorepo layers
nodes.rationale: Backend: models, serializers, services, viewsets, consumers, management commands. Frontend: route pages, feature components, hooks, API clients, shared UI. Cross-cutting: middleware, auth guards, env, Docker, migrations.

nodes.label: Module dependency flow
nodes.rationale: Route or ViewSet points at a thin orchestrator hook or service, which points at deep modules and an API client or serializer.

nodes.label: IHCS module conventions
nodes.rationale: Prefer backend/apps/<app>/services/ for Django deep logic, DRF serializers for shape and services for rules, Next.js admin domain/ or lib/, and extending middleware or AdminAuthGuard. README describes this repo as Next.js only, so the Django and DRF lines may be leftover convention.

nodes.label: Module sketch anti-patterns
nodes.rationale: Avoid one big PR with no seams, a deep module that imports MUI or an ORM, skipping the modify list, and a module-per-file reflex.

nodes.label: PRD template
nodes.rationale: Copy this structure into issues/<filename>.md after Phases 3–4. Status starts as Draft — agreed in PRD session.

nodes.label: P0 P1 P2 requirements
nodes.rationale: Must-have rows are P0 and include a rationale and a decision reference. Should-have is P1. Could-have is P2.

nodes.label: Implementation module map
nodes.rationale: Confirmed Phase 4 sketch: module, layer, Create/Modify/Extend, responsibility, deep flag, test approach, and dependencies, plus a mermaid dependency diagram.

nodes.label: PRD product field
nodes.rationale: The template product placeholder lists IHCS website, Email Signatures, Digital Signage, Cross-cutting, or Other. That list is what the file says. It does not name Care Bear Daycare.

nodes.label: Requirement to module traceability
nodes.rationale: Each requirement such as R-001 maps to one or more module IDs such as M-001.

nodes.label: Deploy Next.js site to Pages
nodes.rationale: On push to main and workflow_dispatch. Permissions are contents read, pages write, and id-token write. Concurrency group pages does not cancel in progress.

nodes.label: Pages build job
nodes.rationale: ubuntu-latest with working-directory frontend. Uses Node 20, Corepack, and a .next/cache key hashed from frontend/yarn.lock and frontend JS/TS sources.

nodes.label: Pages deploy job
nodes.rationale: Needs the build job. Environment github-pages. Deploys with actions/deploy-pages@v5.

nodes.label: Package manager detection
nodes.rationale: If frontend/yarn.lock exists, use yarn install. Else if frontend/package.json exists, use npm ci. Otherwise fail.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages base path
nodes.rationale: actions/configure-pages@v5 sets static_site_generator next, but next.config.js wraps config in withPlugins(), which the injector cannot rewrite. The build also sets GITHUB_PAGES and NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH.

nodes.label: Pages public env
nodes.rationale: The build writes NEXT_PUBLIC_HOST=https://www.niico.com, NEXT_PUBLIC_COMPANY=NIICO Millwork Group LTD., NEXT_PUBLIC_ESTABLISHED=2020, and a placeholder NEXT_PUBLIC_MUI_X_LICENSE_KEY. The host and company conflict with the Care Bear Daycare brand.

nodes.label: frontend/out Pages artifact
nodes.rationale: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 uploads frontend/out after next build.

nodes.label: Test Frontend workflow
nodes.rationale: Triggers are workflow_dispatch and push to main when frontend/** or this workflow file changes. Concurrency cancels in progress. Default working directory is frontend. LOCK_FILE is frontend/yarn.lock.

nodes.label: Frontend lint job
nodes.rationale: The only job enables Corepack, caches yarn, runs yarn install --immutable, then yarn lint. The job if also allows pull_request, which the on block does not include.

nodes.label: pre-commit-hooks
nodes.rationale: Pinned at v3.4.0. Hooks: trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-yaml, check-added-large-files, and check-json.

nodes.label: prettier hook
nodes.rationale: mirrors-prettier v2.2.1 with args --config frontend/.prettierrc.

nodes.label: Care Bear Daycare Brand Reference
nodes.rationale: Design-system reference for mockups. Values match the live marketing theme. This is the current product identity.

nodes.label: Warm playful daycare
nodes.rationale: Cream paper, deep teal ink, caramel accent, and a little coral.

nodes.label: Marketing color tokens
nodes.rationale: Page cream #FBF4E8, muted #F3E6D2, dark cream #E4D0B4, scrollbar hover #D4BC9C, ink #0B3C43, ink hover #14525C, teal pressed #082E34, caramel #D9924F, coral heart #CF5133, paper #FFFCF7. Paragraphs use ink at about 0.78 alpha.

nodes.label: Staff dark teal charcoal
nodes.rationale: STAFF_DARK_BACKGROUND #0E272C, paper #122E34, muted #16353B, elevated #1E454C, staff light elevated #F7EBDC. Dark primary is light teal #9FD4DE. Dark secondary is light caramel #F0C48A. LUXURY_GRADIENT_SX keeps the two-layer structure and retints it.

nodes.label: Semantic colors are not the brand
nodes.rationale: Error, warning, success, and info stay on existing MUI hues. Tailwind chips from red through stone are for status chips and data grids, not marketing pages.

nodes.label: Nunito marketing type
nodes.rationale: Nunito via next/font/google, weights 400, 500, 600, and 700, display swap. Uppercase is for small eyebrows only. Headings and buttons are not forced uppercase.

nodes.label: homeMontserrat Nunito alias
nodes.rationale: The export is still named homeMontserrat, and HOME_LANDING_FONT_FAMILY and SPLASH_FONT_MONTSERRAT still point at it. The face is Nunito.

nodes.label: Hero pill buttons
nodes.rationale: heroCtaSx outlined pills: radius 999, weight 600, tracking 0.04em, text-transform none, white text and border. Hover fills a light white wash.

nodes.label: Cream interior nav
nodes.rationale: Interior nav sits on cream with ink links. The hover underline grows left to right in 0.35s, white on the hero and WEBSITE_INK on interior pages. Desktop nav starts at xl.

nodes.label: Full-color Care Bear logo
nodes.rationale: Full-color PNG on transparency: /imgs/logos/logo.png on the hero and /imgs/logos/logo_hori.png in the nav. Do not invert, brightness-filter, or flatten it.

nodes.label: Contact frosted glass
nodes.rationale: Contact still uses the frosted glass panel over photography from design-studio-glass.js. Leave that treatment alone. It is not the daycare page style.

nodes.label: Marketing cream scrollbar
nodes.rationale: Track #FBF4E8, thumb #E4D0B4, hover #D4BC9C, radius 100px. Keep frontend/styles/marketing-interior.css in sync with WEBSITE_SCROLLBAR_*.

nodes.label: Marketing layout grid
nodes.rationale: MUI 8px spacing. Breakpoints xs 0, sm 600, md 900, lg 1200, xl 1536. Desktop nav at xl. Form pages go two-column at lg. Interior content max width is about 880px.

nodes.label: Brand do and don't
nodes.rationale: Use cream, paper, deep teal, caramel, spare coral, Nunito, pill buttons, and the full-color logo. Do not bring back the millwork palette (taupe #DBD1C0, near-black #0a0a0a, warm brown charcoal), wide-track uppercase headings, square marketing buttons, an inverted logo, Tailwind chip hues as brand colors, or glass fields restyled as pills.

nodes.label: Care Bear Daycare
nodes.rationale: Marketing site for Care Bear Daycare, a small boarding hotel for dogs. Public pages cover overnight suites, supervised daycare, and outdoor play. Stays are booked on Rover, and visit requests go out by email.

nodes.label: Public marketing pages
nodes.rationale: Routes: / Home, /about About, /how-a-stay-works How a stay works, /gallery Gallery, /contact Contact.

nodes.label: Rover booking URL
nodes.rationale: Book a stay opens the Rover profile via ROVER_BOOKING_URL in frontend/consts/routes.js. That URL is a placeholder until the real profile is set.

nodes.label: Daycare consultation email
nodes.rationale: Contact opens a mail message to contact@carebeardaycare.ca with the subject daycare consultation.

nodes.label: Next.js marketing stack
nodes.rationale: Frontend is Next.js 15 (App Router), React 18, MUI 5, and Yarn 4. Local runtime is Docker Compose with Caddy in front of the Next.js container.

nodes.label: Docker Compose local dev
nodes.rationale: docker compose up --build --remove-orphans serves http://127.0.0.1:3010. The frontend container runs yarn dev on port 3000. Caddy publishes port 3010. Outside Docker: cd frontend && yarn install && yarn dev.

nodes.label: Website App Router layout
nodes.rationale: frontend/ is the Next.js app. Marketing pages live under frontend/src/app/(website)/. docker-compose.yml and Caddyfile are the local reverse proxy and the frontend service.

nodes.label: BSD 3-Clause license
nodes.rationale: BSD 3-Clause. See LICENSE.

nodes.label: frontend service
nodes.rationale: Builds frontend/Dockerfile.local, sets WATCHPACK_POLLING=true, and mounts ./frontend at /code with anonymous volumes for /code/node_modules and /code/.next.

nodes.label: Caddy reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Image caddy:latest, depends on frontend, publishes 3010:3010, and mounts ./Caddyfile at /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.

nodes.label: care-bear-daycare
nodes.rationale: Project name care-bear-daycare, version 1.0.0.

nodes.label: node:latest image
nodes.rationale: images.NODE is node:latest.

nodes.label: python:latest image
nodes.rationale: images.PYTHON is python:latest. README describes a Next.js and Caddy stack and does not mention Python.
